items.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: I started working with Asleep at the Wheel, Don McLean, Lou Rawls, Steve Goodman, Peter Allen, and I made what I think are some very interesting, very good records.

ctx.x: When you left Atlantic did you try to take any of those people with you?

Rahsaan and I went to Warner Brothers for a minute, Fathead was at Warner Brothers for a minute. But that was kind of it. I went off into another thing. I had had a really bad experience making that first Bette Midler record. They threw me off it and then the cuts that I made became the hits and then they wanted me to get back together and that really shattered me. ‘Cause with Nesuhi, he never changed what I did. But with Midler, Ahmet got involved and then all kinds of people that couldn’t find their way across…
You’ve done a lot of fantastic reissues. You must have a lot of patience. You don’t strike me as a real patient person but that’s my own observation.
